title: Generated files and previews
summary: Open Artifacts from this run on a task to find its generated files. Image cards can also appear in the answer; other files have preview and download controls. The run center remains.
html:
Generated files and previews

Open Artifacts from this run on a task to find its generated files. Image cards can also appear in the answer; other files have preview and download controls. The run center remains available when a run has no files or its files were deleted. Use its category filter to browse images, data, documents, interactive files, archives and other content.

Show images in the conversation

Enable Show images, directly below Auto scroll in Conversation view, to see image artifacts from each run. It is off by default and saved separately for each conversation. Unlinked images appear in a gallery; images already shown in the answer are not duplicated. This works in standard and immersive views on desktop and mobile. Click any preview to expand it in a lightbox, then press Escape or Close to return. Downloads remain available with the toggle off. Sensitive or unsupported images keep their existing preview restrictions.

Mermaid diagram files (.mmd or .mermaid) are drawn the same way: inline in the answer and in the gallery while Show images is on, and behind View while it is off. The diagram uses the current theme and redraws when the theme changes. In the lightbox, Source switches to the diagram text. A diagram that cannot be drawn shows the renderer's message together with its source. The renderer is bundled with the application, so diagrams render without internet access.

Mermaid code blocks in an answer (fenced as ```mermaid) follow the same preference. With Show images on, the diagram replaces the code block; Show source under it reveals the code again. With it off, the code block stays and View diagram opens the diagram in the lightbox. A block is drawn only after its closing fence arrives, so a streaming answer never shows a half-drawn diagram.

View or download a file

View or Preview opens supported images, diagrams, data and text in a dialog. PDF opens in a separate browser tab. HTML previews can use their own inline interactions, but external resources are blocked, so a page that depends on a CDN or remote API may look incomplete. Close the dialog to return to its original control.

Text and data previews show a bounded sample. CSV displays up to 50 data rows and 32 columns, with long cells clipped. A sampled count is labeled At least; truncation, invalid JSON and deeply nested JSON have explicit notices. Mermaid diagrams render from the same 64 KiB sample; larger diagram files are download-only. Image, PDF and HTML previews also have size ceilings. Download retrieves the original registered version even when its preview is unavailable.

Files marked Sensitive have no thumbnail or preview. Authorized downloads still contain their original bytes, and Download all includes sensitive files. Model redaction settings do not remove values from those downloads or turn ordinary browser previews into redacted copies.

Versions and Download all

A changed file is saved as another version. Existing answer links keep their original artifact identity; they do not silently follow the newest bytes. Earlier versions are labeled in the run center.

Download all creates a ZIP containing the latest version of each logical file path and artifact-manifest.json, which describes the included identities, hashes and versions. If a latest file is unavailable or the export exceeds its configured limit, download the available individual files instead. ZIP filenames may be adjusted to prevent unsafe paths or collisions during extraction.

Pending or unavailable files

Collection can remain pending after the producing command has finished, especially when its Gateway is unavailable or writing has not settled. Retry collection retries the transfer using the original execution target; it does not rerun the command or ask the model to regenerate the file. Choosing another Gateway later does not move that earlier output.

A missing preview can be a format/size restriction, a loading failure or an unavailable stored version. Try the original download where it remains available. An Artifact unavailable message can also reflect deletion, lost source output, scope restrictions or failed byte-integrity checks. A saved link alone does not guarantee that the file is still retained.

Retention

The run center's Artifact retention for this conversation control saves one conversation policy: follow conversation retention, 7/30/90 days, or keep until deleted. Age limits use the latest artifact update. Saving a policy does not immediately delete files; cleanup waits for its maintenance opportunity and protects active, resumable or referenced work.

Deleting chat history or archiving a task does not itself delete its generated files. Explicit artifact/everything deletion and protected cleanup have separate ownership rules. See Configuration and storage for deletion controls and Artifacts architecture for the implementation and recovery boundaries.
